In Theorem~\ref{thm:sparse}, we have shown that we need at most $2 T \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{PC}} \right\|_0$ local sets to represent the piecewise-constant template of $\mathbf{x}$. Since we use at most $K$ eigenvectors in each local set, we obtain the results in Theorem~\ref{thm:PPL}.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate a bandlimited signal by bandlimited signals on the subgraphs, splitting the Laplacian quadratic form over pieces and cut edges. The error per piece is bounded by the (K+1)-th subgraph eigenvalue, and Corollary-type counting bounds the number of local sets.

nodes.name: Detection of piecewise-smooth signals with D_LSPS
nodes.statement: We consider statistically testing the null and alternative hypothesis, \begin{eqnarray*} H_0 &:& \mathbf{y} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 \mathrm{I}), \\ H_1 &:& \mathbf{y} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}, \sigma^2 \mathrm{I}),~\mathbf{x} \in \mathrm{PBL}_{\mathrm{V}_L}(C,K). \end{eqnarray*} We solve the following optimization problem \begin{eqnarray*} \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* & = & \arg \min_{\mathbf{a}} \left\| \mathbf{y} - \mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS} \mathbf{a} \right\|_2^2 \\ && {\rm subject~to~} \left\| \mathbf{a} \right\|_0 \leq 2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0, \end{eqnarray*} by using the matching pursuit algorithm. We reject the null if $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} > \tau$. Set $\tau = \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$. If $$ \frac{\left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2}{\sigma} \geq C \sqrt{2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0 } \sqrt{8 \log(\frac{KNT}{\delta})}, $$ where $C = \max_{ |\Omega| \leq 2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0 } \left\| (\mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS})_{\Omega} \right\|_2 /(1- \sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm par}}) $. Then under $H_0$, $\mathbb{P}({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$, and under $H_1$, $\mathbb{P} ({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$.
conclusions: Then under $H_0$, $\mathbb{P}({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$, and under $H_1$, $\mathbb{P} ({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Thresholding the largest sparse-coding coefficient over D_LSPS detects piecewise-bandlimited signals with error probability delta when SNR exceeds the stated level.
nodes.label: thm:PPL_Detect

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 12
nodes.statement: Under the null, we have $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{e}}^* \right\|_{\infty} < \sigma \sqrt{2 \log( KNT /\delta)}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. We set $\tau = \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$ to control the type 1 error. For the alternative, $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} \geq \left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^* \right\|_{\infty} - \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$ with probability $1-\delta$. In Theorem~\ref{thm:PPL}, we see that it is feasible to have $\left\| \mathbf{x} - \mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS} \mathbf{a}_\mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2 \leq \epsilon_{\rm par} \left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2$ with $\left\| \mathbf{a}_\mathbf{x} \right\|_0 = 2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0$. We then have \begin{eqnarray*} \left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^* \right\|_{\infty} \geq \frac{ \left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^* \right\|_{2} }{ \sqrt{ \left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^* \right\|_0 } } \geq \frac{ 1 - \sqrt{ \epsilon_{\rm par}}}{ \left\| (\mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS})_{\Omega} \right\|_2 \sqrt{ 2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0 } } \left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2, \end{eqnarray*} where $\Omega$ is the support of zero elements in $\mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^*$. Then, we force the lower bound of $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} $ to control the type 2 error.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian max bound controls type 1 error; for type 2, the sparse approximation from Theorem 11 lower-bounds the largest coefficient.

nodes.name: Local-set dictionaries beat windowed graph Fourier transform on piecewise-smooth signals
nodes.statement: We see that the local-set-based dictionaries perform better than the windowed graph Fourier transform; local-set-based piecewise-smooth dictionary is slightly better than local-set-based piecewise-constant dictionary; even though the windowed graph Fourier transform is solid in theory, provides highly redundant representations and is useful for visualization, it does not well approximate complex  graph signals.
conclusions: the local-set-based dictionaries perform better than the windowed graph Fourier transform

nodes.name: Upper bound via Hilbert-Schmidt norm
nodes.statement:
We first show $\left\| \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega}  \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma} \right\|_2 \leq \left\| \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \right\|_{\infty}  \sqrt{ |\Gamma|\cdot |\Omega|}$.
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&	( \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \mathbf{x} )_s
\ = \ \sum_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{V}_{s,k} \left( \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \mathrm{U}_{k,i} x_i \right)
\\
& = &  \sum_{i \in \Gamma}  \left(   \sum_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{V}_{s,k} \mathrm{U}_{k,i} \right) x_i
\ = \ \sum_i q(s,i) x_i,
\end{eqnarray*}
   where
   \begin{equation*} q(s,i) = 
  \left\{ 
    \begin{array}{rl}
      \sum_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{V}_{s,k} \mathrm{U}_{k,i}, & i \in \Gamma;\\
      0, & \mbox{otherwise}.
  \end{array} \right.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathbf{y}^{(i)}$ be a graph signal with $y^{(i)}_s = q(s,i)$. Then, $( \widehat{\mathbf{y}^{(i)}} )_k = {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{U}_{k,i}$. We then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&	\left\| \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \right\|_{2}^2
 \ \leq \  \left\| \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \right\|_{\rm HS}^2
\\
& = & \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{s} |q(s,i)|^2 
\ =  \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \left\| \mathbf{y}^{(i)} \right\|_2^2
\\
& = & \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \left\| \widehat{ \mathbf{y}^{(i)} } \right\|_2^2
\ = \  \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{k} \left( {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{U}_{k,i} \right)^2
\\
& \leq & \left\| \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \right\|_{\infty}^2 \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{k} {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} 
\ = \   \left\| \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \right\|_{\infty}^2 |\Gamma| \cdot |\Omega|.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Show ||V_Omega U_Omega I_Gamma||_2 <= ||U_Omega||_inf sqrt(|Gamma||Omega|).

nodes.name: Kernel representation
nodes.statement_short: Write V_Omega U_Omega I_Gamma x as a kernel q(s,i) applied to x.

nodes.name: Bound the Hilbert-Schmidt norm
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{y}^{(i)}$ be a graph signal with $y^{(i)}_s = q(s,i)$. Then, $( \widehat{\mathbf{y}^{(i)}} )_k = {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{U}_{k,i}$. We then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&	\left\| \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \right\|_{2}^2
 \ \leq \  \left\| \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \right\|_{\rm HS}^2
\\
& = & \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{s} |q(s,i)|^2 
\ =  \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \left\| \mathbf{y}^{(i)} \right\|_2^2
\\
& = & \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \left\| \widehat{ \mathbf{y}^{(i)} } \right\|_2^2
\ = \  \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{k} \left( {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} \mathrm{U}_{k,i} \right)^2
\\
& \leq & \left\| \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \right\|_{\infty}^2 \sum_{i \in \Gamma} \sum_{k} {\bf 1}_{k \in \Omega} 
\ = \   \left\| \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \right\|_{\infty}^2 |\Gamma| \cdot |\Omega|.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the operator norm by the Hilbert-Schmidt norm and use Parseval on each column.

nodes.name: Lower bound via concentration
nodes.statement_short: Show the operator applied to x keeps norm at least 1 - (eps_Omega + eps_Gamma).

nodes.name: Distance of x to its projection
nodes.statement:
We then show that $\left\|  \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma} \mathbf{x}  \right\|_2 \geq 1 - (\epsilon_{\Omega}  +  \epsilon_{\Gamma} )$.
Based on the assumption, we have
   \begin{eqnarray*}
 &&  \left\| \mathbf{x} - \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma}  \mathbf{x}  \right\|_2
   \\
& = &   \left\| \mathbf{x} - \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma} \mathbf{x} \right\|_2  + \left\| \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma} \mathbf{x} -  \mathrm{V}_{\Omega} \mathrm{U}_{\Omega} \mathrm{I}_{\Gamma} \mathbf{x}  \right\|_2 
	\\
& \leq & \epsilon_{\Omega}  +  \epsilon_{\Gamma}. 
   \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Use vertex and spectrum concentration to bound ||x - V U I x||.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Unit norm plus the triangle inequality gives the lower bound.

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement_short: Combine upper and lower bounds to get the uncertainty inequality.

nodes.name: Children are less smooth than parent
nodes.statement:
We first show that the sum of variations of two children local sets is larger than the variation of the parent local set.
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \mathrm{S}_{\Delta, 0} (S_{i+1,2j-1}) + \mathrm{S}_{\Delta, 0} (S_{i+1,2j})  
\\
& = & \frac{1}{ |S_{i+1,2j-1}| }\left\| \Delta {\bf 1}_{ S_{i+1,2j-1} } \right\|_0 + 
\frac{1}{ |S_{i+1,2j}| }\left\| \Delta {\bf 1}_{ S_{i+1,2j} } \right\|_0
\\
& \stackrel{(a)}{ \geq } &  \frac{1}{ |S_{i,j}| }  \left(  \left\| \Delta {\bf 1}_{ S_{i+1,2j-1} } \right\|_0 + \left\| \Delta {\bf 1}_{ S_{i+1,2j} }  \right\|_0 \right)
\\
& \stackrel{(b)}{\geq} &  \frac{1}{ |S_{i,j}| }\left\| \Delta {\bf 1}_{S_{i,j}} \right\|_0 \ = \ \mathrm{S}_{\Delta, 0}  (S_{i,j}),
\end{eqnarray*}
where $(a)$ follows from that the cardinality of the the parent local set is larger than either of its children local sets and $(b)$ follows from that we need to cut a boundary to partition two children local sets.
nodes.statement_short: Two children have summed variation at least that of the parent.

nodes.name: Sum over the level
nodes.statement: Since every local set in the $i$th level has two children local sets in the $i+1$th level and every local set in the $i+1$th level has a parent local set in the $i$th local, we sum them together and obtain Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth}.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the parent-children inequality over all sets of level i.

nodes.name: Unit norm
nodes.statement:
First, we show each vector has norm one.
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \left\| \sqrt{ \frac{|S_1| |S_2|}{|S_1|+|S_2|}} \left(  \frac{1}{ | S_1 |} {\bf 1}_{S_1} - \frac{1}{| S_2 |} {\bf 1}_{S_2}\right)  \right\|_2^2 
\\
&  \stackrel{(a)}{=} & 
|S_1|  \left( \sqrt{\frac{|S_1| |S_2|}{|S_1|+|S_2|}}  \frac{1}{ | S_1 |}  \right)^2 +  |S_2|  \left( \sqrt{\frac{|S_1| |S_1|}{|S_1|+|S_2|}}  \frac{1}{ | S_2 |}  \right)^2 
\\
& = & 1,
\end{eqnarray*}
where $(a)$ follows from that $S_1 \cap S_2 = \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the norm of each wavelet vector using disjoint supports.

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.statement_short: Show pairwise orthogonality of the wavelet vectors.

nodes.name: Orthogonal to the constant vector
nodes.statement_short: Each vector sums to zero, so it is orthogonal to the normalized constant vector.

nodes.name: Two node-set pairs
nodes.statement: Each other individual vector is generated from two node sets. Let $S_1, S_2$ generate $\mathbf{w}_i$ and $S_3, S_4$ generate $\mathbf{w}_j$.
nodes.statement_short: Let w_i, w_j be generated by S1,S2 and S3,S4.

nodes.name: Two possible configurations
nodes.statement: Due to the construction, there are only two conditions, two node sets of one vector belongs to one node set of the other vector, and all four node sets do not share element with each other.
nodes.statement_short: Supports are either nested or disjoint by construction.

nodes.name: Nested case
nodes.statement_short: Nested supports: w_j sums to zero on a set where w_i is constant.

nodes.name: Disjoint case
nodes.statement: For the second case, the inner product between  $\mathbf{w}_i$ and $\mathbf{w}_j $ is zero because their supports do not match.
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint supports give zero inner product.

nodes.name: Spanning
nodes.statement: Third, we show that $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$ spans $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^N$. Since we recursively partition the node set until the cardinalities of all the node sets are smaller than 2, there are $N$ vectors in $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$.
nodes.statement_short: There are N orthonormal vectors, so they span R^N.

nodes.name: Activated edges
nodes.statement: When an edge $e \in {\rm Supp}(\Delta \mathbf{w})$, where Supp denotes the indices of nonzero elements, we call that the edge $\mathbf{e}$ is activated by the vector $\mathbf{w}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define when a basis vector activates an edge.

nodes.name: At most T activations per edge
nodes.statement: Since each edge is activated at most once in each decomposition level, so each edge is activated by at most $T$ basis elements.
nodes.statement_short: Each edge is activated at most once per level, hence at most T times.

nodes.name: Count nonzero coefficients
nodes.statement_short: Sum activations over inconsistent edges to bound the nonzero coefficients.

nodes.name: Errors need inconsistent edges
nodes.statement: The error happens only when there exists at least one inconsistent edge in a community.
nodes.statement_short: Errors only occur in local sets containing an inconsistent edge.

nodes.name: At most K erroneous communities
nodes.statement: Since there are $K$ inconsistent edges, we make errors in at most $K$ communities.
nodes.statement_short: K inconsistent edges affect at most K local sets.

nodes.name: Worst case
nodes.statement: The worst case is that each error is made in the one of the largest $K$ communities.
nodes.statement_short: Worst case: errors fill the K largest local sets.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: The main idea is that we approximate a bandlimited signal in the original graph by using bandlimited signals in subgraphs.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate a global bandlimited signal by bandlimited signals on subgraphs.

nodes.name: Bandlimited space
nodes.statement: Based on the eigenvectors of graph Laplacian matrix, we define the bandlimited space, where each signal can be represented as $\mathbf{x} = \mathrm{V}_{(K)} \mathbf{a},$ where $\mathrm{V}_{(K)}$ is the submatrix of $\mathrm{V}$ containing the first $K$ columns in $\mathrm{V}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the Laplacian bandlimited space x = V_(K) a.

nodes.name: Split the quadratic form
nodes.statement_short: Bandlimited implies x^T L x <= lambda_K x^T x; split it into subgraph Laplacians plus cut edges.

nodes.name: Reduction to subgraphs
nodes.statement: Thus, $\{\mathbf{x}: \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L} \mathbf{x} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} \}$ is a subset of $\bigcup_{S_c}  \{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x}  \}$; that is, any  total pairwise smooth graph signal in the whole graph can be precisely represented by total pairwise smooth graph signals in the subgraphs.
nodes.statement_short: Globally smooth signals are piecewise smooth on the subgraphs.

nodes.name: Per-piece approximation error
nodes.statement:
In each local set, when we use the bandlimited space 
$\{ \mathbf{x}: \mathbf{x} = {\mathrm{V}_{S_c}}_{(K)} \mathbf{a} \}$ to approximate the space $\{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq   c \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \}$, the maximum error we suffer from is $c \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x}_{S_c} / \lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$, which is solved by the following optimization problem,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&	\max_{\mathbf{x}}  \left\|  \mathbf{x} - \mathrm{V}_{S_c} \mathrm{V}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2
	\\
&&	{\rm subject~to:}~   \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x} \leq   c  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x}.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Bandlimited approximation on a piece costs at most c x^T x / lambda_{K+1}.

nodes.name: Total error epsilon_par
nodes.statement:
In other words, in each local set, the maximum error to represent $ \{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x}   \}$ is 
$(\lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x})/\lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$. Since all the local sets share the variation budget of $\lambda_K \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x}$ together, the maximum error we suffer from is $\epsilon_{\rm par} \left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2 = (\lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x})/ \min_{S_c} \lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sharing the variation budget across pieces gives the constant epsilon_par.

nodes.name: Count atoms
nodes.statement: In Theorem~\ref{thm:sparse}, we have shown that we need at most $2 T \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{PC}} \right\|_0$ local sets to represent the piecewise-constant template of $\mathbf{x}$. Since we use at most $K$ eigenvectors in each local set, we obtain the results in Theorem~\ref{thm:PPL}.
nodes.statement_short: At most 2T||Delta x_PC||_0 local sets, K eigenvectors each.

nodes.name: Type 1 error
nodes.statement: Under the null, we have $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{e}}^* \right\|_{\infty} < \sigma \sqrt{2 \log( KNT /\delta)}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. We set $\tau = \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$ to control the type 1 error.
nodes.statement_short: Under H0 the largest coefficient stays below tau with probability 1 - delta.

nodes.name: Alternative: noise perturbation
nodes.statement: For the alternative, $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} \geq \left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{x}}^* \right\|_{\infty} - \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$ with probability $1-\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Under H1 the coefficient is at least the noiseless one minus tau.

nodes.name: Lower bound from Theorem 11
nodes.statement_short: Use the sparse approximation of Theorem 11 to lower-bound the largest noiseless coefficient.

nodes.name: Type 2 error
nodes.statement: Then, we force the lower bound of $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} $ to control the type 2 error.
nodes.statement_short: Require the lower bound to exceed the threshold, controlling type 2 error.

nodes.name: Initialize root local set
First bisection
nodes.statement_short: Split the whole node set into two local sets spanning V_1.

nodes.name: Recursive bisection
nodes.statement:
We then
recursively partition each larger local set into two smaller local
sets.

nodes.name: Level-i partition
nodes.statement_short: Each level-i set S_{i,j} is split into S_{i+1,2j-1} and S_{i+1,2j}.

nodes.name: Stop at singletons
nodes.statement:
When
$|S_{i,j}| \leq 1$, $S_{i+1,2j-1} = S_{i,j}$ and $S_{i+1,2j} =
\emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Sets of size at most one are carried down unchanged.

nodes.name: Fiedler vector
nodes.statement: We first obtain the graph Laplacian matrix of a local set and compute the eigenvector corresponding to the second smallest eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian matrix.

nodes.name: Median threshold
nodes.statement: We then set the median number of the eigenvector as the threshold

nodes.name: Split by threshold
nodes.statement: we put the nodes whose corresponding values in the eigenvector are no smaller than the threshold into a children local set and put the nodes whose corresponding values in the eigenvector are smaller than the threshold into the other children local set.

nodes.name: Maximum spanning tree
nodes.statement: we first obtain the maximum spanning tree of the subgraph

nodes.name: Balance node
nodes.statement: then find a balance node in the spanning tree.

nodes.name: Remove balance node and split
nodes.statement: We remove the balance node from the spanning tree, the resulting largest connected component form a children local set and the other nodes including the balance node forms the other children local set.

nodes.name: Random centers and assignment
nodes.statement: We first randomly select 2 nodes as the community center and assign every other node to its nearest community center based on the geodesic distance.

nodes.name: Recompute centers and reassign
nodes.statement: We then recompute the community center for each community by minimizing the summation of the geodesic distances to all the other nodes in the community and assign node to its nearest community center again.

nodes.name: Iterate to convergence
nodes.statement: We keep doing this until the community centres converge after a few iterations.

nodes.name: Initialize stack and basis
nodes.statement: initialize a stack of node sets $\mathbb{S}$ and a set of vectors $\mathrm{W}$

nodes.name: Push root
nodes.statement: push $S = \mathcal{V}$ into $\mathbb{S}$

nodes.name: Add constant vector
nodes.statement: add $\mathbf{w} = \frac{1}{ \sqrt{|S|}} {\bf 1}_S$ into $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$
nodes.statement_short: Add the normalized all-ones vector.

nodes.name: While loop over large sets
nodes.statement:
while the cardinality of the largest element of $\mathbb{S}$ is bigger than $1$  \\ 
    &~pop up one element from $\mathbb{S}$ as $S$ \\
    &~partition $S$ into two disjoint connected sets $S_1, S_2$ \\
    &~push $S_1, S_2$ into $\mathbb{S}$ \\
    &~add $\mathbf{w} = \sqrt{ \frac{|S_1| |S_2|}{|S_1|+|S_2|}} \left(  \frac{1}{|S_1|} {\bf 1}_{S_1} - \frac{1}{|S_2|} {\bf 1}_{S_2}\right)$ into $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$
nodes.statement_short: Repeat while some set on the stack has more than one node.

nodes.name: Pop
nodes.statement: pop up one element from $\mathbb{S}$ as $S$

nodes.name: Partition
nodes.statement: partition $S$ into two disjoint connected sets $S_1, S_2$
nodes.statement_short: Call a graph partition algorithm (spectral clustering, spanning tree or 2-means).

nodes.name: Push children
nodes.statement: push $S_1, S_2$ into $\mathbb{S}$

nodes.name: Add wavelet vector
nodes.statement: add $\mathbf{w} = \sqrt{ \frac{|S_1| |S_2|}{|S_1|+|S_2|}} \left(  \frac{1}{|S_1|} {\bf 1}_{S_1} - \frac{1}{|S_2|} {\bf 1}_{S_2}\right)$ into $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$
nodes.statement_short: Add the normalized Haar-like vector of the split.

nodes.name: Return
nodes.statement: {\bf return} $\mathrm{W}_{\rm LSPC}$

nodes.name: Partition into m leaf local sets
nodes.statement: Instead of obtaining a full decomposition tree, we partition the local sets until we obtain $m$ leaf local sets.

nodes.name: Split largest first
nodes.statement: For the local sets in the same level of the decomposition tree, we first partition the one that has the largest number of nodes.

nodes.name: Choose centers
nodes.statement: For each leaf local set, we choose a center that has the minimum summation of the geodesic distances to all the other nodes in the leaf local set.

nodes.name: Sample centers
nodes.statement: We use those centers for the $M$  leaf local sets as the sampled set.

nodes.name: Assign sampled values
nodes.statement_short: Assign each center's sample to its whole leaf local set.

nodes.name: Solve regularized fit
nodes.statement:
For harmonic functions, we consider
\begin{eqnarray*} \mathbf{x}' =  &  \arg \min_{\mathbf{t}} & \left\| \mathbf{x}_\mathcal{M} - \mathbf{t}_\mathcal{M}  \right\|_2^2 + \mu \left\| \Delta \mathbf{t} \right\|_2^2,
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\left\| \Delta \mathbf{t} \right\|_2^2 = \mathbf{t}^T \mathrm{L} \mathbf{t}$ and $\mathrm{L}$ is the graph Laplacian matrix.

nodes.name: Round to constants
nodes.statement: When we obtain the solution, we assign each coefficient to its closest constant in $\mathbf{x}$.
